name: AB0805-T3
title: AB08X5 ultra-low-power real-time clock, I2C (AB0805) or SPI (AB0815), QFN-16 3 x 3 mm
summary: A real-time clock family drawing as little as 14 nA, built on Ambiq Micro's SPOT subthreshold CMOS. It keeps time from a 32.768 kHz crystal or an internal RC oscillator, which can be calibrated against the crystal automatically, and holds 256 bytes of RAM, alarms, a countdown timer and a watchdog. A power control block switches to a backup source on VBAT when VCC fails. The AB0805 talks I2C, the AB0815 SPI; both come in a 3 x 3 mm QFN-16 and run from 1.5 V to 3.6 V over -40 °C to 85 °C.

circuits.title: Battery-backed RTC
circuits.description: The RTC and an MCU share the system supply on VCC. A battery or supercapacitor sits on VBAT through a series resistor; the backup source's own resistance plus this resistor should total 1.5 kΩ. When the system supply is lost the RTC moves to VBAT on its own and keeps time and RAM contents on a very small current; while VCC is present the internal trickle charger keeps the supercapacitor or rechargeable cell charged. A 32.768 kHz crystal hangs across XI and XO. The MCU reads and writes the RTC over the serial bus, and FOUT/nIRQ drives the MCU's active-low interrupt input.

parts.note: total series resistance of the backup path, source ESR included

notes: The link to the MCU is the family's I2C/SPI port; on the AB0805 it is SCL and SDA, each with a pull-up.
FOUT/nIRQ is open drain and takes a pull-up.

circuits.title: RTC gathering interrupt sources
circuits.description: The RTC collects several interrupt sources and hands the MCU a single interrupt line on FOUT/nIRQ. Two digital signals enter on WDI and EXTI; an analog level enters on VBAT, where the internal comparator watches it. Internal timers and alarms join the same interrupt. The RTC runs from the system supply on VCC with a 32.768 kHz crystal across XI and XO, and the MCU talks to it over the serial bus.

operation.text: A host reaches every function through offset-mapped registers, over I2C on the AB0805 or SPI on the AB0815. Functions fall in three groups: baseline timekeeping (32.768 kHz crystal oscillator, counters from hundredths of a second to centuries plus weekday, alarms on all counters, countdown timer with repeat, programmable clock output from 32.768 kHz down to once a year, leap-year handling); advanced timekeeping (an RC oscillator, digital calibration, autocalibration, watchdog, input and output options); and power management (VBAT switchover, external interrupt monitoring, battery threshold detection, an analog comparator). 256 bytes of low-leakage RAM hold data on backup power. Every input has a Schmitt trigger.

XT mode runs from the 32.768 kHz crystal for the best accuracy at about 55 nA. RC mode runs from a temperature-compensated RC oscillator with the crystal stopped, about 14 nA, where lower accuracy is acceptable. Autocalibration mode runs from the RC oscillator and trims it against the crystal from time to time, every 8.5 or 17 minutes or on software command, for about 22 nA on average with accuracy close to XT mode.

Both oscillators are tuned digitally: the crystal to within ±2 ppm and the RC oscillator to within ±16 ppm at a given temperature. The RC oscillator is factory calibrated to 128 Hz at 25 °C and 2.8 V. Autocalibration is specified from -10 °C to 60 °C; outside that span the RC frequency may leave the ±12 % calibration range, autocalibration then fails and sets ACF, and the crystal should become the clock source.

XI and XO take a 32.768 kHz tuning-fork crystal; the load capacitor and resistor are integrated. Pin capacitance is 1 pF typical inside the part and 1 pF typical on the board. The oscillation allowance is 270 kΩ minimum, 320 kΩ typical. The XT oscillator failure detection frequency is 8 kHz typical.

The power control block watches VCC. When VCC falls below VCCSWF with VBAT above VBATSW,MIN, the part moves to the VBAT Power state and keeps time and RAM; it returns to VCC when VCC climbs past VCCSWR (about 70 mV hysteresis). The switch is guaranteed only for VCC falling no faster than VCCFS, and VBAT must stay at least 200 mV above VCC to remain on backup. Leaving POR needs VCC above VCCST regardless of VBAT. In the VCC Power state VBAT draws 0.5 nA to 0.6 nA typical.

The source on VBAT should present 1.5 kΩ in all, its own ESR plus an added series resistor if needed. Without a backup source VBAT is tied to VSS. VBAT can instead carry an analog level for the comparator, whose falling and rising thresholds are set by the BREF code (0111, 1011, 1101 or 1111) and which is recommended for -20 °C to 70 °C.

FOUT/nIRQ is held low from power-up until the part leaves reset and the interface can be used. A valid POR needs VCC held low long enough: typically 0.1 s at 25 °C, rising to 10 s at -40 °C. FOUT then goes high about 0.5 s after VCC rises at 25 °C (20 s at -40 °C), and the crystal oscillator starts roughly 0.4 s later.

FOUT/nIRQ, nIRQ2 and nTIRQ are open drain. OUT1S and OUT2S choose what FOUT/nIRQ and nIRQ2 carry: a static bit, the square wave, the combined interrupt, the alarm interrupt or, on nIRQ2, the timer interrupt. nTIRQ on the AB0805 carries only the timer interrupt.

NC pins stay open. The thermal pad, pin 17, connects to VSS. WDI and EXTI have no internal pull resistors and must not float; tie them to VCC or VSS when unused. SCL and SDA each need a pull-up; nCE on the AB0815 should have one. A 47 pF ceramic capacitor from AF to VSS improves autocalibration accuracy.
The AB0805 has an I2C port at 10 kHz to 400 kHz. The AB0815 has a 3-wire or 4-wire SPI port up to 2 MHz. The interface works over VCC 1.5 V to 3.6 V.
Lead-free, RoHS compliant, rated MSL 1 to JEDEC J-STD-020D.1, and suited to lead-free reflow at up to 260 °C.
